intervals.label: laboratories established
intervals.note: INFN states 1955; some other sources give a different founding year (1954); the INFN page is followed.
intervals.quote: Established in 1955, the National Laboratories of Frascati are the top Italian research facility for studying nuclear and subnuclear physics with accelerators.

operator_text.quote: INFN has four National research Laboratories that host large equipment and infrastructure provided to the national and international scientific community.

summary.plain: The Italian National Institute for Nuclear Physics' accelerator laboratory near Rome. It built the first matter-antimatter collider, AdA, then ADONE, and now runs DAΦNE, an electron-positron collider that produces phi mesons for the KLOE experiments.
summary.technical: INFN-LNF, Frascati (Rome); electron synchrotron (1959), AdA (1961), ADONE (1969) and DAΦNE (a φ-factory e⁺e⁻ collider at 1.02 GeV centre-of-mass energy), with the Beam Test Facility and SPARC_LAB.
